players.note: Nakobe Dean went off in Week 11, racking up six solos, six assists, one sack, two tackles for loss, and one pass defended. The LB1 overall and in fppg, Dean has four splash weeks to his name and is locked in as a top-three option regardless of opponent. Fire Nakobe up for a plus Week 12 matchup against the Cleveland Browns.

Jordyn Brooks stepped up in Week 11, racking up two solos, six assists, one sack, and one tackle for loss. Brooks has seven spike weeks on the season, but has recorded one in five straight games, pushing him back into the top-10 mix. Fire Brooks up as an LB1 play for a plus Week 12 matchup against the New York Jets.

Fred Warner was excellent in Week 11, tallying four solos, four assists, one tackle for loss, and one pass defended. Warner has remained an elite IDP weapon in 2026 and checks into Week 12 as the LB7 in fppg. Continue to count Warner as a top-10 option for a plus Week 12 matchup against the Seattle Seahawks.

Arvell Reese stepped up in Week 11, tallying four solos, three assists, and one tackle for loss. Reese has been one of the more explosive IDP producers at the position and is considered the runaway favorite for Defensive Rookie of the Year. The LB4 in fppg, Reese appears to be locked in as a top-five option for years to come. Fire him up as just that for a plus Week 12 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts.

Alex Singleton stayed hot in Week 11, racking up three solos, eight assists, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one pass defended. Singleton has been an elite IDP producer and checks into Week 12 as the LB5 in fppg. Continue to count the Broncos linebacker as a top-three option regardless of opponent.

Jacob Rodriguez was elite in Week 11, tallying eight solos, five assists, one interception, and one pass defended. Rodriguez has four splash weeks and one spike week under his belt, but has combined them with two true duds. His variance keeps him out of the top-10 discussion and instead relegates him to the top-15 conversation. Treat him as just that for a plus Week 12 matchup against the New York Jets.

Carson Schwesinger was at it again in Week 10, reeling off eight solos, five assists, and one tackle for loss. The LB6 in fppg, Schwesinger is locked in as a top-12 option regardless of opponent, and should be treated as such for a plus Week 11 matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders.

CJ Allen stayed hot in Week 11, notching seven solos, nine assists, and one tackle for loss. Allen has recorded four straight spike weeks since becoming a starter for the Colts, bullying his way into top-15 conversation in the process. Count him as just that for a pus Week 12 matchup against the New York Giants.

Josiah Trotter was excellent in Week 12, notching eight solos and six assists. Trotter is the LB12 in fppg on the season, but has slipped into being more of a top-15 option than a top-12 play since Week 1. Count Josiah as a top-15 option for a plus Week 12 matchup against the Carolina Panthers on Monday Night Football.

Jamien Sherwood showed up in Week 11, reeling off eight solos, three assists, and one forced fumble. Sherwood has been one of the more consistent LB2 options and is locked in as a top-25 play for a plus Week 12 matchup against the Miami Dolphins.

Jeremiah Trotter was excellent in Week 11, tallying nine solos and four assists. Jeremiah has been excellent when given starter snaps, consistently producing at an upside LB2 level or better. Trotter should be counted as a top-25 option for a plus Week 12 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys.

Ernest Jones showed up in Week 10, recording five solos and five assists. The LB11 in fppg, Jones is locked in as a weekly LB1 play. Start him with confidence for a plus Week 12 matchup against the San Francisco 49ers.

Quay Walker was excellent in Week 11, racking up seven solos and four assists. Quay checks into Week 12 as the LB2 in fppg and makes for a strong top-25 option during the byes. However, with no byes this week, Walker is more of a top-30 play/elite LB3 than the LB2 we count him as when teams have the week off. Tap Quay as a top-30 play for a plus Week 12 matchup against the Cleveland Browns.

Tyrel Dodson was excellent in Week 11, going off with five solos, three assists, one fumble recovery, one interception, and one pass defended. Dodson has started the last three games with Bobby Okereke sidelined and could have more starts left for fantasy managers. Okereke missed practice all of last week and is on the wrong side of questionable after being an early rule out for Week 11. Dodson offers top-25 upside when he is getting starts, making him worth the speculative add where available. Fire Dodson up as a top-30 option for a plus Week 12 matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

Quincy Williams stepped up in Week 10, tallying five solos, four assists, and one pass defended. Quincy has been a strong LB2 option this season and checks into Week 10 as the LB20 in fppg. Fire up the Browns linebacker as a top-25 play for a plus Week 12 matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders.

Trenton Simpson finally showed up in Week 11, notching five solos and five assists. Simpson emerged as an LB1 option early in the season but has since slipped back down to the LB3 realm. This was his first spike week since Week 5, and with no teams on bye, he cannot be considered part of the top-25 conversation. Count the Ravens linebacker as a top-36 option for a plus Week 12 matchup against the Houston Texans.

Ventrell Miller stepped up in Week 11, tallying four solos, three assists, and two tackles for loss. Ventrell has been a bit of a disappointment from an IDP perspective, but has started to heat up a bit with two of his best three fantasy games coming in his last two contests. Feel free to count Miller as a LB4 option for a plus Week 12 matchup against the Tennessee Titans.

Jack Gibbens stepped up in Week 11, notching six solos and four assists. Gibbens played 73 percent of the snaps against Kansas City. He was already leading in snap share over Cody Simon, but when Simon went down with a calf injury, Gibbens snaps ballooned. This will remain a frustrating platoon when both are healthy, but it once again looks like Gibbens is the preferred linebacker to roster. With that said, Gibbens was not much more than an LB3 before the time split and is now more of an LB4/5 who should only be considered for a flex spot for Week 12.

Malcolm Rodriguez showed up in Week 11, racking up four solos, two assists, 0.5 sacks, and one pass defended. Rodriguez has been seeing extra snaps with Jack Campbell on IR and has at least one more game of fantasy relevance with Campbell guaranteed to be sidelined for Week 12. Rodrigo is an LB5/flex2 type at best with no teams on bye but still has enough upside to start against the Chicago Bears on Thursday afternoon. Make the add where needed.

Jihaad Campbell showed up in Week 11, tallying five solos, two assists, and one tackle for loss. Jihaad played 81 percent of the snaps with Zack Baun sidelined and should offer LB3 with LB2 upside value for as long as Baun remains on the shelf (at least until Week 15). Jihaad has flashed top-15 upside but has not shown enough consistency to count as anything more than a top-36 option with zero teams on bye. Add and start Jihaad where possible.

David Bailey was at it again in Week 11, racking up two solos, three assists, two sacks, two tackles for loss, one forced fumble, and one pass defended. Bailey is up to 9.5 sacks, with four of them coming in two of his last three games. Now the DL1 in fppg, Bailey is locked in as a top-three option for a saliva-inducing Week 12 matchup against the Miami Dolphins. Start Bailey everywhere.

Harold Perkins got the start in Week 10 and responded with six solos, one assist, and one tackle for loss. Perkins has just four spike weeks on the season, but three of them have come in his last four games when he was filling in for the injured Divine Deablo. Divine had some time to heal up during the bye week, but if he cannot go in Week 12, Perkins becomes a must-start LB3 play.

Mike Green stayed sizzling in Week 11, racking up four solos, one assist, two sacks, and two tackles for loss. The Ravens pass rusher is up to 7.5 sacks on the season, with four of them coming in his last two games. For context, Green now has the same number of sacks as T.J. Watt and more than Byron Young, Maxx Crosby, Nik Bonitto, and failed trade acquisition Trey Hendrickson. Green is a top-25 play as long as he is burning hot and should be treated as such for a plus Week 12 matchup against the Houston Texans.

Greg Rousseau was at it again in Week 11, tallying three solos, two sacks, and two tackles for loss. Rousseau is up to 10 sacks, with four of them coming in three of his last four games. Now the DL5 in fppg, the Bills edge rusher can be counted as a top-five option as long as he is cooking. Start Rousseau everywhere.

Danny Stutsman stepped up in Week 11, recording three solos, six assists, one interception, and one pass defended. It was the second straight spike week for Stutsman, who could be poised to make a couple more starts with Pete Werner sidelined with a hamstring injury he suffered in Week 10. Stutsman is an LB4/5 type for the zero bye Week 12 but will be back in the LB3/4 conversation for Week 13. Don't break the bank for Stutsman, as we do not yet know how long Werner will be sidelined, but we can comfortably project at least one more start for Danny given the nature of soft-tissue injuries. Make the add where needed ahead of a plus Week 12 matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals.

Boye Mafe went off in Week 11, exploding for four solos, one assist, three sacks, and three tackles for loss. Suddenly up to 9.5 sacks following his massive breakout on Monday Night Football, Boye has at least one sack in six of his last seven games. It is impossible not to count him as part of the DL1 conversation while he is this hot. Treat him as just that for a plus Week 12 matchup against the New Orleans Saints on Sunday afternoon. Start Mafe everywhere.

Josh Hines-Allen stepped up in Week 11, reeling off three solos, two assists, one sack, one tackle for loss, one forced fumble, and one pass defended. Allen has been more name than game for fantasy purposes as he has struggled in the sack department this season and sits at just three sacks. Treat him as a top-36 option at best for a plus Week 12 matchup against the Tennessee Titans.

Jadeveon Clowney stayed hot in Week 11, racking up three solos, one assist, one sack, and two tackles for loss. Jadeveon is up to 5.5 sacks on the season, with four of them coming in his last three games. Danielle Hunter (hamstring) is already considered doubtful for this Sunday and is set to miss his third straight game. Clowney appears poised to get at least one more start for the Texans, making him an intriguing DL2 option for a tasty Week 12 matchup against the Baltimore Ravens. Start the Texans pass rusher wherever possible.

Byron Young showed up in Week 10, tallying three solos, one sack, and two tackles for loss. Young has been quieter than expected this season, but is starting to turn it on. For now, count the Rams edge rusher as a top-20 option for a plus Week 12 matchup against the Green Bay Packers on Thanksgiving Eve.

Abdul Carter was elite in Week 11, racking up three solos, one assist, two sacks, and two tackles for loss. Carter has been a pressure monster all season and now finally has a reasonable sack total to show for it. Carter has remained part of the top-25 conversation more based on talent and pressures than actual fantasy production but is now at least worthy of being part of the discussion for reasons other than upside.

Alex Highsmith showed up in Week 11, tallying two solos, two sacks, two tackles for loss, and one forced fumble. Highsmith is up to 5.5 sacks on the season, but this was his first full sack since all the way back in Week 2, and coincided with Nick Herbig being sidelined. Unfortunately, Highsmith had his ankle rolled up on after his second sack of the first quarter and was ruled out for the rest of the game. Now, on a short week, Highsmith is no lock to even suit up. Jack Sawyer will once again see an expanded role if Highsmith is ruled out as expected. With that said, Highsmith is still worth a stash where possible, as the Steelers have a favorable schedule down the stretch that could help him produce at a DL2 level if he is healthy.

Justin Barron stepped up in Week 11, recording six solos and three assists for the Dallas Cowboys. Barron got the tap over DeMarvion Overshown when Dee Winters was forced to leave the game with injury. Barron had been a special teams only player for most of the season and is likely headed back to the bench with Dee Winters already logging a limited session on a Tuesday in a short week. There is a chance the Cowboys play it cautious, but with the division on the line and the New York Giants surging, Winters may take the field, even on only a few days' rest. Look elsewhere for Week 12 if Winters is active, as expected.

Jonathan Cooper was excellent in Week 11, posting two solos, one assist, two sacks, two tackles for loss, and one pass defended. Cooper is now up to 2.5 sacks on the season, with all of them coming in his last two games. Cooper has played over 60 percent of the snaps in each game since his return and should provide DL2-level production down the stretch. Tap Cooper as a DL3 with obvious DL2 upside for a plus Week 12 matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Black Friday.

Nolan Smith stepped up in Week 11, racking up three solos, two assists, one sack, and one tackle for loss. Smith now sits at a healthy six sacks on the season but just played a season low in snaps for a full game. Jonathan Greenard is getting healthier every week, and Jalyx Hunt remains the preferred option against the run. With that said, Nolan has a sack in four straight games and should see his snaps stay in the 50 to 60 percent range as long as he stays hot. Tap Smith as a DL3/4 with DL2 upside for a plus Week 12 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys on Thanksgiving.

Montez Sweat stepped up in Week 11, tallying two solos, one sack, and two tackles for loss. Sweat is up to four sacks on the season, with a sack in two of his last three games. Sweat has disappointed on the season as a whole, but with Jeffery Simmons now commanding all the attention, he has started to get going. For now, continue to treat him as a DL3, but he no longer poses the waiver wire floor risk. Start Sweat where needed.

Jack Sawyer stepped up in Week 11, racking up three solos, one sack, and one tackle for loss on 73 percent of the snaps. Sawyer saw extra snaps with Nick Herbig inactive and Alex Highsmith injured in the first quarter. The sack was the first of the season for the Ohio State alum, who appears poised to see an expanded role again on Friday. He may not start as Nick Herbig was estimated as a limited participant on Tuesday, but should still see enough snaps to warrant lineup consideration. Tap Sawyer as a DL3/4 option for a plus Week 12 matchup against the Denver Broncos.

James Houston showed up in Week 11, racking up four solos, two sacks, and two tackles for loss. Houston is up to 3.5 sacks, with all of them coming in three of his last four games. Now second on the team in sacks, Houston also famously led the Cowboys in sacks last season up until Week 12, despite the team barely giving him snaps. The Cowboys edge rusher has seen his snaps spike since the Cowboys demoted defensive coordinator Christian Parker and makes for a solid DL4 option as long as he is producing. Treat him as such for a plus Week 12 matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles on Thursday afternoon.

Lukas Van Ness showed up in Week 10, reeling off two solos, two assists, 1.5 sacks, and one tackle for loss. Van Ness is up to six sacks, with 2.5 of them coming in two of his last three games. Van Ness is once again a comfortable top-30 option and should be treated as such for a plus Week 12 matchup against the Los Angeles Rams.

DeMarcus Lawrence was back at it in Week 10, racking up five solos, one assist, one sack, and two tackles for loss. Both of Lawrence's sacks have come in his last two games, putting him back in the mix as a DL3/4 option. Treat him as just that for a plus Week 12 matchup against the San Francisco 49ers. Add Lawrence where needed if you can afford to stash him through the bye.

David Walker stepped up in Week 11, generating three solos, two assists, one sack, and two tackles for loss. Now up to five sacks on the season despite a strict rotational role, Walker leads the Buccaneers in sacks, tackles for loss, and QB hits. His usage has kept him out of the conversation in 12 team leagues, but now that he has more sacks than Danielle Hunter, Montez Sweat, and Josh Hines-Allen, it is time to take him seriously, even in 12 team leagues. Tap Walker as a DL3/4 option for Week 12 and beyond, but be cognizant of the snap-based floor.

DJ Wonnum stepped up in Week 11, racking up five solos, one sack, one tackle for loss, one forced fumble, and one pass defended. Wonnum is starting to heat up for the Lions and is now up to an impressive seven sacks, with a sack in each of his last two games. Wonnum should continue to see all the snaps he can handle with Aiadan Huthcinson lost for the season and is a solid DL3 with DL2 upside. Fire Wonnum up as a top-30 option for a plus Week 12 matchup against the Chicago Bears on Thursday afternoon.

Trevor Nowaske showed up for the Detroit Lions in Week 11, tallying two solos, two assists, one sack, and two tackles for loss. Nowaske is an off-ball linebacker who sees some edge snaps on passing downs and finally got home against Tampa Bay. The sack was the first of the season for Nowaske, who has been seeing more snaps since Aidan Hutchinson was lost for the season. With that said, he is not yet on the fantasy radar outside of 32 team leagues and can safely be ignored for Week 12 of the fantasy football season.

Derick Hall stepped up in Week 10, reeling off two solos, one assist, one sack, and two tackles for loss. Hall is up to four sacks on the season and should be treated as a DL4 option for a plus Week 12 matchup against the San Francisco 49ers.

Jonathan Greenard was back at it in Week 11, recording one solo, one sack, and one tackle for loss. Greenard has registered a sack in back-to-back games and has steadily seen his snap share increase to where it now sits in the 50 percent range. Despite his DL1 pedigree, Greenard remains more of a DL3/4 due to both the rotation he is currently mired in and the fact that the Eagles have no reason to play him more than they feel comfortable with due to the season already being in the tank. Tap Greenard as a top-40 option for a plus Week 12 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys.

Princely Umanmielen showed up in Week 11, notching three solos, one assist, 1.5 sacks, and one tackle for loss. Princely started the season hot but had been kept off the sack sheet since Week 4. He now sits at 4.5 sacks on the season and makes for a strong DL3 option, even with no byes for Week 12. Treat Umanmielen as just that for a plus Week 12 matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Monday Night Football.

Dante Fowler was back at it in Week 10, tallying two solos, one assist, one sack, and two tackles for loss on just 34 percent of the snaps. Fowler has just two sacks on the season, but both of them have come in his last two games. He remains more DL5 than DL4 and is better viewed as a depth piece than someone you want to start for Week 12, but if you find yourself in a bind, you can certainly do worse than an edge rusher who has shown signs that he is starting to heat up and just played a season high in snaps.
